<a id="ExitStatus"></a>

### Exit status

`ExitStatus` · `src/system.ts:13`

What a command returns to the system that started it: zero if it succeeded, something else otherwise.

Source: POSIX.1-2017, exit(); ISO C, EXIT_SUCCESS and EXIT_FAILURE · `https://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9699919799/functions/exit.html`

| Constant | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `success` | `0` | The command succeeded (EXIT_SUCCESS) |
| `failure` | `1` | The command failed (EXIT_FAILURE) |

- Maintained by: trame
- Serves: [A published value is cited, not copied](product.md#CitedNotCopied)
- Used by: [Node's command line](tooling.md#NodeProgramCommands)

<a id="NodeCli"></a>

### Node.js command line and child processes

`NodeCli` · `src/system.ts:95`

How a program is run by Node: a module imported before it, the warnings silenced; how a child shares the terminal.

Source: Node.js documentation: Command-line API (--import, NODE_NO_WARNINGS), child_process (options.stdio) · `https://nodejs.org/api/cli.html`

| Constant | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `importFirst` | `--import` | Imports a module before the program: a loader, say |
| `enabled` | `1` | The value that turns an environment flag on (NODE_NO_WARNINGS=1) |
| `inherit` | `inherit` | A child process writes on the same terminal as its parent |
| `ignore` | `ignore` | A child process reads nothing from its parent |
| `pipe` | `pipe` | The parent reads what a child process writes |

<a id="NodeEvents"></a>

### Node.js events

`NodeEvents` · `src/system.ts:77`

The events a program listens to on Node's streams, child processes, requests and process.

Source: Node.js documentation: stream.Readable ('data', 'close', 'error'), ChildProcess ('exit', 'close'), process ('unhandledRejection') · `https://nodejs.org/api/events.html`

| Constant | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `data` | `data` | A readable stream gives a chunk of what it reads |
| `close` | `close` | A stream, a request or a child process is closed: nothing more will come |
| `exit` | `exit` | A child process ended, with its exit code |
| `error` | `error` | A stream failed |
| `unhandledRejection` | `unhandledRejection` | A promise was rejected and nothing waited for it |

<a id="NodeModuleSpecifiers"></a>

### Node.js module specifiers

`NodeModuleSpecifiers` · `src/system.ts:114`

How an import names a module: a relative specifier starts from the importing file; any other names a package, a built-in module (node:fs) or an import map entry (#trame/kernel).

Source: Node.js documentation, ECMAScript modules: Terminology (relative, bare and absolute specifiers); Packages: Subpath imports · `https://nodejs.org/api/esm.html#terminology`

| Constant | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `current` | `./` | Opens a relative specifier from the importing file's directory |
| `parent` | `../` | Opens a relative specifier from the directory above |
| `separator` | `/` | Separates the segments of a specifier, as in a URL path, whatever the platform |
| `packages` | `node_modules` | The directory where the packages a project imports are installed |
| `imports` | `#` | Opens a specifier the package's own import map resolves (subpath imports): #std/algebra |
| `pattern` | `*` | Stands for the rest of a subpath, in an entry of an import map and in its target |

- Maintained by: trame
- Serves: [A published value is cited, not copied](product.md#CitedNotCopied)

<a id="Posix"></a>

### POSIX signals and errors

`Posix` · `src/system.ts:28`

The signals a program forwards to the one it runs, and the error that says the reader of its output went away.

Source: POSIX.1-2017, Base Definitions: <signal.h> (SIGINT, SIGTERM), <errno.h> (EPIPE), § 4.13 Pathname Resolution (dot) · `https://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9699919799/basedefs/signal.h.html`

| Constant | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `currentDirectory` | `.` | The directory a path starts from: a command in it is run as ./name |
| `interrupt` | `SIGINT` | The interruption asked from the terminal (Ctrl-C) |
| `terminate` | `SIGTERM` | The polite request to end |
| `brokenPipe` | `EPIPE` | Writing to a pipe that nobody reads any more (the output piped into head, say) |
